items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: We ended up Red Balaban led the band pretty much three nights and I led it three. Most of the time early on he led it five or six nights

ctx.x: And you would just go up — would you go up on the stand and call the tunes as you felt, playing to the crowd somewhat?
That’s right. We ended up Red Balaban led the band pretty much three nights and I led it three. Most of the time early on he led it five or six nights and it evolved that I would

have the band on Monday nights. I tried changing it a little bit on Monday nights toward the end and had a few modern players, Lew Tabackin I remember working with him one night, Effie Resnick who had gotten quite modern on trombone. I was trying to present a little bit of a more modern flavor, but that was just my indulging myself. But yeah, we’d just go up on the stand and not give it that much thought. I’d look down the songlist, say hey we’ll do this, and if we had requests we’d play the requests. It was…
